A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same anchor-selection study. All 23 pages in each version, including Appendices A–F, are readable and support comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on Arena-Hard-v2.0 and AlpacaEval, including ranking correlations, anchor informativeness, sensitivity analyses, and power-analysis simulation results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental and simulation results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The anchor-based ranking procedures, win-rate and Bradley–Terry aggregation, and small-sample informativeness estimation remain identical. No algorithm or model component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Arena-Hard-v2.0 and AlpacaEval data and task coverage. No dataset, domain, or evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets remain unchanged, including 22 anchor/competitor models for Arena-Hard and 11 for AlpacaEval. Both retain the same five judges and comparisons with quadratic and human rankings.

E3.justification: The dataset sizes, judge settings, prompt source, ranking metrics, and sample-size and multiple-anchor evaluation protocols are unchanged in Section 3, Section 5, and the appendices.

E4.justification: Both retain the same win-rate-distribution analysis, sample-size sensitivity tests, multiple-anchor experiment, and informativeness-estimation study. No supplementary analysis is added, removed, or revised.

E5.justification: The stated 30 repetitions, 40 shuffled anchor permutations, standard-deviation summaries and shaded bands, significance thresholds, and power-analysis procedures remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–10 and Figures 1–22 retain the same numerical results and findings. For example, Table 1 reports quadratic-ranking correlations of 0.957 for Gemma 3 27B Instruct and 0.818 for o3 in both versions.

T1.justification: The ranking and informativeness definitions, transitivity assumptions, sample-size reasoning, and power-analysis mathematics are unchanged. No formal result or derivation is added or corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about extreme anchors, the advantages of mid-performing anchors, anchor versus judge selection, and insufficient benchmark sizes.

C2.justification: The explanations involving signal saturation and informative samples, practical recommendations, and Limitations section are unchanged, including qualifications about transitivity, human-ranking agreement, and model-pool-relative mediocrity.

D1.justification: Code and data access information, judge defaults and prompt source, the human-ranking retrieval date, and the power-analysis code in Listing 1 remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, and bibliography are unchanged. Reference text moves because of reflow, without adding or removing works or revising research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short Acknowledgements section after Limitations, crediting Israel Science Foundation grant 2912/25, and updates the arXiv version/date annotation. The scientific prose and narrative organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 removes printed page-number footers and reflows the references and opening appendix text following the acknowledgement. Figures, tables, captions, and graphical displays remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The acknowledgement slightly improves funding transparency, while removing printed page numbers slightly reduces navigation convenience. The scientific argument, results, appendices, and reproducibility information are unchanged, so these editorial differences produce no meaningful net change in overall quality.
